project.objective: When and where did Cornelius Hermanus Zacharias Booysen of Pretoria, Transvaal, South Africa die?

questions.question: What was the date and place of death of Cornelius Hermanus Zacharias Booysen of Pretoria, Transvaal, South Africa?
questions.rationale: The research objective is to determine when and where this individual died. Date and place of death are co-located facts typically found together in civil death registrations, burial records, and obituaries. South African civil registration in the Transvaal was established in the late 19th century; FamilySearch holds digitized death registers for this jurisdiction. This single question targets the complete death event.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All plan items across two research plans (pl_001 superseded, pl_002 active) are completed. The principal Transvaal Civil Death collection (2998108, covering 1869-1954) was searched with multiple strategies: broad surname+given name queries, targeted birth-year-range + death-year-range queries, and a spousal filter (Daniel/Bester). NDR church registers (collection 2155416), FamilySearch cemetery records, and FindAGrave were also searched. Ancestry was attempted but access was unavailable. Source attachment checks and a targeted record_read of a specific ARK were completed. Original death certificate images could not be examined due to OpenRouter not being configured. person_record_matches is disabled in this benchmark run. The indexed Transvaal Civil Death collection may not capture every death, but all name-indexed records for GWDS-CKP's exact name and plausible birth/death year ranges are exhausted.
exhaustive_declaration.stop_criteria: All plan items in pl_001 and pl_002 are completed or skipped. No additional repositories or record types identified that could be searched with available access. Index search exhausted; original images unavailable.

items.rationale: South Africa, Transvaal, Civil Death, 1869-1954 (collection 2998108) is the primary source for death date and place. ~557 Pretoria-city volumes are 92-99% name-indexed and searchable by name. Death certificates record full name, age, sex, birthplace, marital status, occupation, place and date of death, residence, place of burial, cause/duration of death, and informant details. Booysen is an Afrikaner surname; Cornelius Hermanus Zacharias is a distinctively triple-barrelled Afrikaner name — a surname-only search followed by first-name filtering should isolate any match. Locality guide loc_001 confirms this collection is the highest-priority source for Pretoria deaths.

South Africa, Civil Death Registration, 1953-1967 (collection 3732506) covers deaths after the Transvaal Civil Death collection ends in 1954. If Cornelius died after 1954, his record will appear here rather than in collection 2998108. Indexed + images; national coverage. Search as fallback if pli_001 returns no match.

South Africa, Transvaal, Probate Records from the Master of the Supreme Court, 1869-1961 (collection 2520237) contains death notices (MHG series). Per locality guide loc_001, Transvaal death notices are essential documents that typically supply age, date and place of death, marital status, names of children, and (when known) names of parents of the deceased — often more genealogically rich than the civil death certificate. 1,870,732 indexed records. First Transvaal death notices created 1873. Even if pli_001 finds the civil certificate, this record provides corroboration and may supply additional facts (burial place, names of survivors).

South Africa, Netherdutch Reformed Church Registers (Pretoria Archive), 1838-1991 (collection 2155416) contains burial entries as well as baptisms and marriages. Booysen is a characteristic Afrikaner surname associated with the Dutch Reformed tradition; a Netherdutch Reformed burial entry would supply the date and place of burial/death and may predate civil registration or supplement it. 75,380 records indexed; 3,049,440 persons. Locality guide loc_001 flags this as especially relevant for Afrikaner surnames.

South Africa, Gauteng, Johannesburg, Cemetery Records, 1840-2019 (collection 4453927) covers the greater Pretoria area with 2,406,245 records and is indexed. Cemetery records supply burial date and place which, for this era, typically coincide closely with date and place of death. Also search the eGGSA Graves Database (http://www.eggsa.org/librarySearch/searchGraves.htm) and Find a Grave (South Africa). Provides independent corroboration of civil/church evidence.

Ancestry holds the 'Transvaal Province, South Africa, Estates Death Notice Index, 1855-1976' — an index to Transvaal death notices complementary to the FamilySearch probate collection (pli_003). Searching here as an external cross-check, particularly useful if the death falls outside the 1869-1961 window of collection 2520237 or if the FamilySearch index missed the entry. Per external_links_search results from loc_001 survey.

The log_001 search found a second unexamined Pretoria candidate: 'Cornelius Booysen, b.1856, d.12 Mar 1940, Pretoria' (ark:/61903/1:1:74GL-7NPZ). This was deprioritized in the initial pass because the 1853-born triple-named candidate appeared to be the subject. Now that the 1853-born candidate is confirmed as GWDS-CKP's grandfather (not GWDS-CKP himself, born 1906), this 1940 candidate warrants immediate record read. The birth year '1856' in the index may be an indexing/OCR error for '1906' (GWDS-CKP's birth year), or this may be a different Cornelius Booysen entirely. Reading the full record will resolve this. This is the highest-priority item because the record is already in hand from the prior search.

Re-search collection 2998108 (South Africa, Transvaal, Civil Death, 1869-1954) for GWDS-CKP with birth year filter 1901-1915 and death year 1934-1954. The original pli_001 search returned the grandfather (born ~1853, died 1925) but did not filter by birth year or death year, so GWDS-CKP's record (born 1906, last known alive Dec 1933) may be in the same collection at a later date. Per loc_001, collection 2998108 covers Pretoria at 92-99% name-index coverage. Use subjectId GWDS-CKP so the ranker scores against the now-enriched tree person with the 1906 birth year context.

Check FamilySearch source attachments and person-record matches for tree person GWDS-CKP. FamilySearch's own matcher may have already linked a death record to this person that parametric name searches missed. Use source_attachments or person_record_matches on GWDS-CKP (a FS-ID person, not a local stub, so the FS matcher has likely run against it). This is a quick lookup that could immediately surface the answer without additional searching.

Search collection 2998108 with spousal name filter: spouseGivenName 'Daniel' (or 'Daniël'), spouseSurname 'Bester'. GWDS-CKP married Daniel Jacobus Bester on 31 Dec 1930. Transvaal civil death records typically name the surviving spouse, so filtering on the distinctive spouse name isolates GWDS-CKP from other Cornelius Booysens. Fallback for pli_008 if that search returns ambiguous results.

Targeted retry of pli_003 with deathYear 1925-1926 and givenName 'Cornelius Hermanus'. 3 results: two entries for Hendrik Hermanus Zacharias Booysen (related to Maria Roos Baumann Booysen estate) and Wessel Cornelius Booysen (b. 1936). None match the subject. All matchScores below 0.01. The Transvaal Probate collection does not appear to contain an indexed death notice for Cornelius Hermanus Zacharias Booysen under his full name. The death notice may exist under an abbreviated name not surfaced by the index, or may not have been filed. Logging as true negative.

Cemetery search (collection 4453927, South Africa Gauteng Johannesburg Cemetery Records) for Cornelius Booysen, death 1920-1930. Single result: 'Booysen' (no given name), burial 25 Sep 1929, Johannesburg, born 1929 — an infant, clearly not the subject. matchScore 0.00013. No cemetery record for Cornelius Hermanus Zacharias Booysen in this collection. True negative.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Date and Place of Death of Cornelius Hermanus Zacharias Booysen (GWDS-CKP)

**Probable conclusion:** Cornelius Hermanus Zacharias Booysen (GWDS-CKP) of Pretoria, Transvaal, South Africa probably died **9 September 1942** at **Standerton, Transvaal, South Africa**.

### Evidence

The FamilySearch-indexed Transvaal Civil Death register (collection 2998108, “South Africa, Transvaal, Civil Death, 1869–1954”) contains one entry — ark:/61903/1:1:7453-9H2M — recording the death of **Cornelius Hermanus Zacharias Booysen**, Male, born 1902, on **9 September 1942** at **Standerton, Transvaal, South Africa**. This is a derivative source (index entry); the underlying original death certificate image was not examined.

The name is an exact, full match to GWDS-CKP in all name elements. The death date is chronologically consistent with GWDS-CKP’s known life events: he married at Pretoria on 31 December 1930 (civil marriage record, source 7VDX-DGP), and his daughter Katrina Johanna Booysen died at Pretoria on 19 December 1933 (civil death record, source 7VDF-1LK), establishing that GWDS-CKP was alive into at least late 1933. The place of death — Standerton, Transvaal — is geographically consistent with the family’s documented Standerton connection; GWDS-CKP’s parents Jan Jonathan Booysen and Catharina Johanna Deysel married at Standerton on 16 May 1905.

### Candidates Evaluated and Rejected

Two other civil death index entries were evaluated and rejected as candidates for GWDS-CKP’s death:

1. **ark:/61903/1:1:74GL-7NPZ** (assertions a_018–a_021) — indexed as “Cornelius Booysen” (truncated name, no middle names), born **1856**, died **12 March 1940**, Pretoria. Rejected on two grounds: (a) the indexed name lacks the middle names “Hermanus Zacharias” present in GWDS-CKP’s full name — while index truncation is possible, this reduces confidence; and (b) the birth year of **1856** represents a **50-year discrepancy** from GWDS-CKP’s tree birth year of 1906, far outside any acceptable tolerance. This is a Weak match — rejected.

2. **ark:/61903/1:1:7H67-92T2** (assertions a_022–a_025) — Cornelius Hermanus Zacharias Booysen, born **1914**, died 22 June 1936 at Johannesburg. The 8-year birth year gap (1914 vs. GWDS-CKP’s 1906) exceeds the ±5-year tolerance for a Moderate identity match. Rejected as a Weak match.

### Unresolved Conflict: Birth Year Discrepancy

The accepted death record (7453-9H2M) gives a birth year of **1902**, while GWDS-CKP’s tree birth year is **1906** — a 4-year discrepancy. This gap falls within the ±5-year tolerance commonly accepted for secondary birth year information on death certificates, where the informant (typically the surviving spouse) often could not confirm the decedent’s exact birth year. Note that GWDS-CKP’s tree birth year of 1906 is itself an unverified pre-existing fact with no source assertion in the current research record; neither value has been confirmed by an original birth or baptism record.

A formal conflict entry could not be created for this discrepancy because the schema requires two source-backed assertions, and the tree birth year of 1906 has no source assertion in research.json. The conflict is addressed analytically in this narrative. The same_person algorithmic score of 0.230 (confidence 2) is low, primarily reflecting the birth year gap and the sparsity of the single-person index record; it does not indicate a qualitative identity conflict independent of the birth year.

This conflict cannot be resolved without examining the original death certificate image (FamilySearch image ARK: ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C9BY-6SH7-M), which was unavailable in this research session.

### Limitations

This conclusion rests on a single derivative source (an index entry). No corroborating independent record confirms this death event. The conclusion is classified **probable** rather than GPS-proved because: (1) the original certificate was not examined; (2) the birth year discrepancy is unresolved; and (3) no second independent source confirms the death date and place. To upgrade to a proved conclusion, researchers should examine the original Transvaal civil death register image and seek a corroborating source such as a burial record, probate file, or newspaper death notice.

quirks: Civil registration in the Transvaal began in 1901; the Transvaal Civil Death collection (2998108) covers 1869-1954 with ~557 digitized volumes for Pretoria city, most at 92-99% name-indexed.

Death notices (MHG series) in the Transvaal probate records (collection 2520237) often contain more genealogical detail than civil death certificates — include names of parents and children of the deceased.
The National Archives of South Africa (NAAIRS) has an online index to Transvaal death notices; use 'MHG' as a search term at http://www.national.archives.gov.za to filter to death notices only.
Records are in Afrikaans and English; spelling was not standardized until the early 20th century — try surname-only searches if a full-name search returns nothing.
For 1899-1902, Transvaal Civil Death records are arranged by Anglo-Boer War internment camp and district, not alphabetically — search by place/camp for that period.

The Netherdutch Reformed Church Registers (Pretoria Archive, collection 2155416) are especially relevant for Afrikaner surnames and include burial entries as well as baptisms and marriages, 1838-1991.
Transvaal Province was dissolved in 1994 into Gauteng, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, and North-West; all records created before 1994 remain organized under the Transvaal jurisdiction.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Pretoria, Transvaal, South Africa (1870–1960)

## Jurisdictional Context

Pretoria city existed under three successive political jurisdictions during the research period:

| Period | Jurisdiction |
|--------|--------------|
| 1855–1902 | Zuid-Afrikaansche Republiek (ZAR / South African Republic) |
| 1902–1910 | Transvaal Colony (British Crown Colony) |
| 1910–1994 | Transvaal Province, Union/Republic of South Africa |

Pretoria served as the administrative capital throughout. In 1994, Transvaal Province was dissolved into four smaller provinces (Gauteng, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, North-West); Pretoria is now in Gauteng. All records created before 1994 remain organized under the old Transvaal jurisdiction.

## Primary Death Records

### South Africa, Transvaal, Civil Death, 1869–1954
- **FamilySearch Collection 2998108** | 961,705 indexed records | 1,081,775 images
- **Access:** Indexed + images — name-searchable at familysearch.org/search/collection/2998108
- **Coverage:** Civil death registrations across the entire Transvaal, including Pretoria, 1869–1954. Records in Afrikaans and English.
- **Content:** Full name, age, sex, birthplace, marital status, occupation, place and date of death, residence, place of burial, cause and duration of death, informant background. Parents' names included if deceased was under age 10.
- **Note:** For 1899–1902, records are arranged separately by Anglo-Boer War internment camp and district.
- **Volume coverage:** ~557 digitized Pretoria-city death certificate volumes (1902–1954) at 92–99% name-indexed.

### South Africa, Civil Death Registration, 1953–1967
- **FamilySearch Collection 3732506** | 709,500 indexed records | 1,226,793 images
- **Access:** Indexed + images
- Covers national deaths post-1954; overlaps with Transvaal Civil Death for 1953–1954.

## Probate Records / Death Notices (Highly Recommended)

### South Africa, Transvaal, Probate Records from the Master of the Supreme Court, 1869–1961
- **FamilySearch Collection 2520237** | 1,870,732 records | 1,516,203 images | Indexed + images
- **Death notices (MHG series):** Essential documents. Typically supply age, date and place of death, marital status, names of children, and (when known) names of parents of the deceased. First Transvaal death notices created 1873.
- **NAAIRS Online Index:** http://www.national.archives.gov.za — search 'MHG' as a term to filter to death notices only. The volume number, reference, and year are needed to obtain a copy (e.g., MHG ref. 33266, Abraham Johannes Kruger, 1917).
- **Ancestry:** 'Transvaal Province, South Africa, Estates Death Notice Index, 1855–1976'

### South Africa, Transvaal, Estate Files, 1950–1993
- **FamilySearch Collection 2144007** | 191,580 images | **Browse-only** (0% name-indexed)
- Must be browsed image by image; no name search available.

## Church Records

### Netherdutch Reformed Church Registers (Pretoria Archive), 1838–1991
- **FamilySearch Collection 2155416** | 75,380 records | 3,049,440 persons | Indexed + images
- Especially relevant for Afrikaner surnames (e.g., Booysen). Contains burial/death entries as well as baptisms and marriages.

### Dutch Reformed Church Registers (Cape Town Archives), 1660–1994
- **FamilySearch Collection 1478678** | 2,890,979 records | Indexed + images
- Also at Ancestry and MyHeritage.

## Cemetery Records

- **Find a Grave – South Africa:** findagrave.com
- **eGGSA Graves Database:** http://www.eggsa.org/librarySearch/searchGraves.htm
- **South Africa Burials** at FindMyPast (subscription)
- **South Africa, Gauteng, Johannesburg, Cemetery Records, 1840–2019** (Collection 4453927) — 2,406,245 records, includes greater Pretoria area.

## External Repositories

- **National Archives of South Africa (NAAIRS):** http://www.national.archives.gov.za
- **Genealogical Society of South Africa (eGGSA):** http://www.eggsa.org
- **South African Genealogy:** http://sagenealogy.co.za

## Languages & Search Tips

- Records are in **Afrikaans and English**. Use the Afrikaans Genealogical Word List when reading originals.
- Spelling was not standardized until the early 20th century — try surname-only searches as a fallback.
- For 1899–1902, search by place/camp rather than surname.
